name: Gmail (MCP — power user)
tagline: MCP-based Gmail integration. ⚠️ Most users should use the native Connect Gmail flow on the Integrations tab instead — it's one click and shares a Google account with Calendar/Contacts.
setup_hint: Doesn't use env vars. Place your Google OAuth Desktop App credentials.json at ~/.gmail-mcp/gcp-oauth.keys.json — the MCP server opens a browser on first run to complete consent and writes the refresh token to ~/.gmail-mcp/credentials.json. Same Google OAuth Client can be reused across Gmail + Calendar MCPs.

name: Google Calendar (MCP — power user)
tagline: MCP-based Calendar integration. ⚠️ Most users should use the native Connect Gmail flow on the Integrations tab — it covers both Gmail + Calendar with one consent.
setup_hint: Set GOOGLE_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/keys.json in the env block above (same Desktop App keys.json you used for the Gmail MCP works here). Then — one-time, interactively — run: `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/keys.json npx -y @cocal/google-calendar-mcp auth`. This opens a browser, completes consent, and writes tokens to ~/.config/google-calendar-mcp/tokens.json. Without that step the MCP probe lists tools but every tool call returns 'No authenticated accounts found'.

name: HubSpot
tagline: Read + write contacts, deals, companies; log calls + notes. Recommended CRM path for the SDR template — most-maintained MCP server in the HubSpot ecosystem.
setup_hint: Create a Private App in your HubSpot portal (Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → Create). Grant scopes: crm.objects.contacts.{read,write}, crm.objects.deals.{read,write}, crm.objects.companies.{read,write}, crm.objects.calls.{read,write}. Copy the generated Access Token and paste it as HUBSPOT_PRIVATE_APP_TOKEN in the env block above. The token is the only auth — no browser OAuth dance.

name: Salesforce
tagline: Query + update Leads, Contacts, Opportunities, log tasks. Alternative to HubSpot for Salesforce-native sales teams.
setup_hint: Salesforce auth is two-factor: SALESFORCE_PASSWORD is your account password; SALESFORCE_SECURITY_TOKEN is the per-user token you reset under Settings → My Personal Information → Reset Security Token (Salesforce emails it to you). Both must be filled in. SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL is only needed if you're on a sandbox or non-standard pod (e.g. https://your-domain.my.salesforce.com).
